opening: We render user-written Markdown with pulldown-cmark (current main branch) through its HTML renderer and also use the offset iterator for source mapping. A few inputs are mishandled.

requirements.m01:
Input with CR line endings in HTML blocks and code blocks is mishandled: parsing renders the block without a final newline). Every line of an HTML or code block should be rendered followed by a newline, whatever the source used (LF, CR or CRLF), the last line included. In an unclosed fenced code block or an unclosed HTML block (comment, 
, and the other kinds that end at a closing marker), a last line that is blank or only spaces and tabs with no line ending is dropped, also inside block quotes and list items. It is a line of the block like any other and should be kept: "```\na\n " renders 
a, a newline, a space and a newline, then 
; a block quote holding an open comment followed by a last ">" line keeps an empty line inside the block. Input that simply ends after a line ending is unchanged.
requirements.m02:
Inside a block quote, a following line indented by four or more columns (for example a tab) and then > is still read as another block quote marker, although that much indentation means it is not one. "> a" followed by a line of a tab and "> b" should render one block quote whose paragraph is a, a newline and the literal text > b:
,

a, a newline, > b

,
. And "> *" followed by a line of a tab and "> b" should render a block quote holding a list with one empty item, followed outside the block quote by an indented code block containing > b:
,
    ,
  • ,
,
, then 
> b and a newline,
.
requirements.m03: With container extensions (and definition lists) enabled, an opening container fence such as :::T on the last line of the input, with no line ending after it, yields events whose source ranges end one byte past the end of the input, so slicing the input with a range panics. Every event's range must lie within the input, also for inputs like "1) :::r" and ":::T  ".
